## About

### Dataset
The dataset is [Florida Counties](https://data.census.gov/table/DECENNIALDHC2020.P3?q=P3&g=040XX00US12$0500000&d=DEC+Demographic+and+Housing+Characteristics).  It is stored in the `data` folder. I will use it while mapping.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pyprojroot import here # this helps us navigate tricky path stuff between local runs and quarto builds

# Load the data using here() with the path from the project root
file_path = here("projects/jessie_project/data/florida_counties.csv") # demographics dataset
df= pd.read_csv(file_path, sep=',')

file_path2 = here("projects/jessie_project/data/allprisons.csv") # prison dataset
df_prison= pd.read_csv(file_path2, sep=',')

```

## Wrangling
### first dataset - county demographics
```{python}
# organizing + formatting columns
df = df.transpose()

df.columns = df.iloc[0]
df = df[1:]
df.reset_index(level=0, inplace=True)

df.rename(columns = {"index": "county"}, 
          inplace = True)

df["county"] = df["county"].str.replace(", Florida", "")

df.head(10)
```

```{python}
# New column for total poc percentage
df["Total:"] = df["Total:"].str.replace(",", "")
df["\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0White alone"] = df["\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0White alone"].str.replace(",", "")
df["per_poc"] = df["\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0White alone"].astype(int)/df["Total:"].astype(int) * 100
```

```{python}
# New DF with fips for graphing
from urllib.request import urlopen
import json
with urlopen('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json') as response:
    counties = json.load(response)


url2 = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv"
df_fips = pd.read_csv(url2, dtype={"fips": str})
fips = df_fips["fips"].iloc[322:389]
fips = fips.reset_index(drop = True)

pp = df["per_poc"]
df_new = {
    "Name": df["county"],
    "fips" : fips,
    "Percentage of POC" : pp
}

df_new = pd.DataFrame(df_new)
```

## second dataset - prison locations

```{python}
rows = df_prison[df_prison["stateshortname"] != "FL"].index
df_prison.drop(rows, inplace=True)
df_prison = df_prison.reset_index(drop = True)
df_prison.head(10)
```

```{python}
name1 = df_prison["name"].iloc[:12]
name2 = df_prison["PrisonName"].iloc[12:]

df_prison[['rev_lon', 'rev_lat']] = df_prison['coordinates_rev'].str.split(',', n=1, expand=True)
df_prison["rev_lon"] = df_prison["rev_lon"].str.replace("(", "")
df_prison["rev_lat"] = df_prison["rev_lat"].str.replace(")", "")


lon1 = df_prison["rev_lon"].iloc[:12]
lon2= df_prison["longitude"].iloc[12:]
lat1 = df_prison["rev_lat"].iloc[:12]
lat2= df_prison["latitude"].iloc[12:]

name = pd.concat([name1, name2], ignore_index=True)
long = pd.concat([lon1, lon2], ignore_index=True)
lat = pd.concat([lat1, lat2], ignore_index=True)

df_location = {
    "Prison Name": name,
    "longitute" : long,
    "latitude" : lat
}
```



## Plot time!

```{python}
# Reading geometry
from pyprojroot import here
import geopandas as gpd
myfile = file_path = here("projects/jessie_project/data/fl_counties.geojson")

# open file for read-only
florida = gpd.read_file(myfile)

```

```{python}
# plot demographics 
import plotly.express as px

fig = px.choropleth(df_new, geojson=florida, hover_data=['Name'],locations='fips', color='Percentage of POC',
                    featureidkey="properties.GEOID",
                    color_continuous_scale="Viridis_r",
                    range_color=(0, 100),
                    labels={"Name": "County Name", 'Percentage of POC':'Percent Nonwhite'}
                    )
fig.update_geos(fitbounds="locations",visible=False)
fig.update_layout(margin={"r":0,"t":0,"l":0,"b":0})

fig.show()
```


This graph is how much of each county is nonwhite, according to the 2020 census. The lighter color is a higher density of nonwhite people. Hovering over the county gives you its fips, its name, and the percentage of nonwhite people. Most counties are above 50% nonwhite, with now obvious trends towards one side of the state. 

It is important to note that Hispanic/Latino is a separate question on the census, and Hispanic/Latino people usually identify as white.

```{python}
# plot location
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig2 = go.Figure(go.Scattermap(
        lat=list(df_location["latitude"]),
        lon=list(df_location["longitute"]),
        mode='markers',
        marker=go.scattermap.Marker(
            size=5
        ),
        text=list(df_location["Prison Name"]),
    ))

fig2.show()
```
